title: Advanced Transformation & Synthesis
description: Master advanced transformation and synthesis for Grade 12 (ISC): all synthesis methods, complex active-passive, conditional transforms and reporting of dialogues — bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Synthesis & Complex Voice Conversions
topics.concept:
Synthesis methods (combining sentences) — revise the full toolkit:

  • Participle: Having finished, he left.
  • Infinitive: too weak to walk; the first to arrive.
  • Relative pronoun / apposition / abstract noun / conjunction.
  • Absolute phrase: The work done, they rested.

Complex active–passive: handle tricky cases:

  • Two objects: They gave him a prize. → He was given a prize.
  • Reporting verbs: People say he is honest. → It is said that he is honest. / He is said to be honest.
  • Modals & perfects: One must do this. → This must be done.
  • Infinitive/imperative: Open the door. → Let the door be opened.

examples.problem: Change the voice: People believe that he stole the money.
examples.solution: It is believed that he stole the money. / He is believed to have stolen the money.

examples.problem: Synthesise (abstract noun): He is honest. Everyone trusts him.

recap: Synthesis: participle, infinitive, relative, apposition, abstract noun, absolute phrase
Two-object passives, reporting-verb passives (It is said / He is said to…)
Modal passive = modal + be + V3; imperative = Let … be + V3

topics.title: Conditional & Degree Transformations
topics.concept:
Conditional transformations:

  • Change type or marker: Work hard, or you will fail. → If you do not work hard, you will fail. → Unless you work hard, you will fail.
  • Inversion: If I had known, I would have helped. → Had I known, I would have helped.

Degree of comparison (a perennial favourite):

  • Superlative ↔ comparative ↔ positive: Iron is the most useful metal = Iron is more useful than any other metal = No other metal is as useful as iron.

so…that ↔ too…to ↔ enough:

  • He is so weak that he cannot walk = He is too weak to walk.
  • She is so clever that she can solve it = She is clever enough to solve it.

Assertive ↔ interrogative ↔ exclamatory: How grand the palace is! = The palace is very grand.

examples.problem: Invert the conditional: If she were here, she would help.
Change to positive degree: Gold is more precious than most other metals.
examples.solution: Very few metals are as precious as gold.

recap: Conditionals: change marker (unless), or invert (Had I…, Were I…)
Degree: superlative ↔ comparative ('any other') ↔ positive ('No other … as … as')

outcomes: Apply all methods of sentence synthesis
Combine and split complex sentences as directed

intro.en: Board papers — especially ISC — reward writers who can reshape a sentence at will: combine, split, change voice, invert, or convert a conditional, all without altering the meaning. This chapter brings together every transformation skill you have learned and pushes it to the level the final exam demands.
intro.hi: बोर्ड पेपर — विशेषकर ISC — उन लेखकों को अंक देते हैं जो किसी वाक्य को इच्छानुसार पुनर्गठित कर सकें: जोड़ना, तोड़ना, voice बदलना, invert करना, या conditional बदलना — और वह भी अर्थ बदले बिना। यह अध्याय आपके सीखे सभी transformation कौशलों को एक साथ लाकर उन्हें अंतिम परीक्षा के स्तर तक ले जाता है।

real_life.situation:
One idea, rewritten four ways:

Original: He was so tired that he could not continue.
Infinitive: He was too tired to continue.
Inversion: So tired was he that he could not continue.
Cause: Being too tired, he could not continue.
real_life.why: Each version keeps the meaning while showing command of a different structure. The exam asks for exactly this flexibility — and the marks go to those who can switch forms cleanly and instinctively.

common_mistakes.right: Had she known, she would have come.

common_mistakes.wrong: It is said that he to be honest.

reading.passage: It is widely believed that perseverance matters more than talent. No other quality is as decisive as persistence. Had the great inventors given up at the first failure, the world would be poorer. They were too determined to quit; indeed, so determined were they that setbacks only spurred them on. In short, success, it is said, belongs to those who endure.

questions.q: Rewrite 'No other quality is as decisive as persistence' in the superlative degree.
questions.answer: Persistence is the most decisive quality.

questions.q: Identify the conditional inversion and restore the 'if' form.
questions.answer: 'Had the great inventors given up…' = 'If the great inventors had given up…'.

questions.q: Rewrite 'so determined were they that setbacks…' without inversion.
questions.answer: They were so determined that setbacks only spurred them on.
